**Explanation (coaching note):**
When your opponent attacks your pawn, don't panic—look for trades that improve your position. Here, capturing with hxg4 forces White to recapture, then your king rushes to h4 to attack the remaining h3 pawn. White's king cannot defend both pawns at once. After Ke5 (trying to stop your king), you capture h3 and reach a winning king-and-pawn endgame. Key lesson: in pawn endgames, calculate king activity and race patterns before defending passively.
